ptolemy.name: Claudius Ptolemy (Κλαύδιος Πτολεμαῖος)
ptolemy.role: Alexandrian mathematician, astronomer, geometer, and cartographer
ptolemy.summary: Author of the Mathematike Syntaxis (Almagest), Planisphaerium, Geography, Harmonics, and Optics; synthesized Greek chord trigonometry, cyclic quadrilateral geometry, spherical Menelaus calculus, and stereographic projection.

syrus.name: Syrus (Σύρος)
syrus.role: Dedicatee of Ptolemy's Almagest, Planisphaerium, and Tetrabiblos
syrus.summary: Addressed directly in the opening sentences of both Almagest I.1 ('ὦ Σύρε') and Planisphaerium §1 ('Jesure' / 'Syrus' via Arabic transcription).

hipparchus.name: Hipparchus of Nicaea (Ἵππαρχος ὁ Νικαεύς)
hipparchus.role: Founder of Greek chord trigonometry and quantitative observational astronomy
hipparchus.summary: Compiled a twelve-book treatise on chords in a circle and established solar/lunar models and the tropical-to-sidereal precession upon which Ptolemy built Book I.

menelaus.name: Menelaus of Alexandria (Μενέλαος ὁ Ἀλεξανδρεύς)
menelaus.role: Geometer and spherical astronomer; author of the Sphaerica
menelaus.summary: Formulated the intrinsic geometry of spherical triangles and the six-quantity transversal theorem (Sphaerica III.1) adapted by Ptolemy in Almagest I.13.

euclid.name: Euclid of Alexandria (Εὐκλείδης)
euclid.role: Author of the Elements, Phaenomena, and Optics
euclid.summary: Provides the deductive backbone of Almagest I.10 and I.13, particularly Elements Books I–IV, Book VI (similar triangles and extreme-and-mean ratio), and Book XIII (regular decagon and pentagon).

apollonius.name: Apollonius of Perga (Ἀπολλώνιος ὁ Περγαῖος)
apollonius.role: The 'Great Geometer'; author of the Conics
apollonius.summary: Proved in Conics I.5 that a subcontrary plane section of an oblique circular cone is a true circle—the geometric foundation of stereographic circle preservation in Ptolemy's Planisphaerium.

archimedes.name: Archimedes of Syracuse (Ἀρχιμήδης)
archimedes.summary: Bounded the circumference-to-diameter ratio between 3 + 10/71 and 3 + 1/7 in Measurement of a Circle; Ptolemy's crd(1°) = 1;2,50 yields pi = 3;8,30 = 377/120 strictly inside Archimedes' interval.

eratosthenes.name: Eratosthenes of Cyrene (Ἐρατοσθένης)
eratosthenes.role: Chief librarian at Alexandria, geographer, and mathematician
eratosthenes.summary: Cited by Ptolemy in Almagest I.12 (Heiberg I, p. 68) alongside Hipparchus for measuring the arc between the tropics as 11/83 of the full meridian circle.

aristotle.name: Aristotle of Stagira (Ἀριστοτέλης)
aristotle.role: Philosopher; author of Metaphysics Book E and Posterior Analytics
aristotle.summary: Cited by name in Almagest I.1 (Heiberg I, p. 5) for dividing theoretical philosophy into physics, mathematics, and theology.

theodosius.name: Theodosius of Bithynia (Θεοδόσιος)
theodosius.summary: Codified the pure solid geometry of great and parallel circles on a sphere prior to Menelaus's trigonometric Sphaerica.

maslama.name: Maslama al-Majrītī
maslama.role: Andalusian astronomer and mathematician in Córdoba
maslama.summary: Revised the Arabic translation of Ptolemy's Planisphaerium and added astrolabe commentary; his recension was translated into Latin at Toulouse in 1143.

hermann.name: Hermann of Carinthia (Hermannus Secundus / Dalmata)
hermann.role: Twelfth-century Latin translator and natural philosopher
hermann.summary: Translated Ptolemy's Planisphaerium from Maslama al-Majrītī's Arabic recension into Latin at Toulouse on 1 June 1143, preserving the treatise after the loss of the Greek original.

commandino.name: Federico Commandino
commandino.summary: Published Ptolemaei Planisphaerium: Iordani Planisphaerium; Federici Commandini Urbinatis in Ptolemaei Planisphaerium Commentarius (Venice: Aldus, 1558), proving stereographic circle-preservation explicitly from Apollonius Conics I.5.

halma.name: Nicolas B. Halma
halma.summary: Edited the Greek text and authored the public-domain French translation Composition mathématique de Claude Ptolémée (2 vols., Paris: Henri Grand, 1813–1816).

heiberg.name: Johan Ludvig Heiberg
heiberg.role: Danish classical philologist and historian of Greek mathematics
heiberg.summary: Established the definitive Teubner critical editions of Claudii Ptolemaei Opera quae exstant omnia: Syntaxis Mathematica (Vol. I.1–I.2, 1898–1903) and Opera Astronomica Minora including Planisphaerium (Vol. II, 1907).

manitius.name: Karl Manitius
manitius.role: German classical scholar and historian of astronomy
manitius.summary: Translated Heiberg's Teubner text of the Almagest into German (Des Claudius Ptolemäus Handbuch der Astronomie, 2 vols., Leipzig: Teubner, 1912–1913).

brahmagupta.name: Brahmagupta
brahmagupta.role: Indian mathematician and astronomer; author of the Brāhmasphuṭasiddhānta
brahmagupta.summary: Generalized cyclic quadrilateral geometry with rational sides, diagonals, and areas, complementing Ptolemy's Theorem on cyclic quadrilaterals.

casey.name: John Casey
casey.role: Irish geometer; author of A Sequel to the First Six Books of the Elements of Euclid
casey.summary: Extended Ptolemy's Theorem to four mutually tangent circles (Casey's Theorem) and systematized circular inversion in modern synthetic geometry.
